title: The integral derived direct image of a constructible complex along a finite-type morphism is constructible
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a $K_0$-morphism (of finite type; separatedness is not assumed) [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an object of the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and let $Rf_{*,n}:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ and
$$
 Rf_*K=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}K_n\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)
$$
be the finite-level and the integral derived direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] being taken of the inverse system with the transition maps specified there. Then $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. More precisely: $Rf_*K$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]; for every $n\geq1$ the finite-reduction comparison $(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\to Rf_{*,n}K_n$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is an isomorphism; $Rf_{*,n}K_n\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]; and if the cohomological supports [def-weil-cohomological-support] of all $K_n$ lie in $[a,b]$, then those of all $Rf_{*,n}K_n$ lie in $[a,b+N]$, where $N$ is an integer (independent of $n$) such that $R^qf_*M=0$ for $q>N$ and every sheaf $M$ of $A_{E,1}$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ (when $K_0$ is algebraically closed, one may take $N=2\dim X$ for nonempty $X$, with Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $N=0$ for empty $X).

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2 (Pushforward), p. 55, with its proof: completeness of $f_*K$ by Lemma 6.5.9 (2), p. 50; $f_*K\otimes_{\widehat R}R/\mathfrak m\simeq f_*(K\otimes_{\widehat R}R/\mathfrak m)$ by Lemma 6.5.11 (1),(3), p. 51 (under a cohomological-dimension bound $d$ for $f_*$ on $R/\mathfrak m$-modules, giving the amplitude $\leq k+m+d+2$ of 6.5.11 (1)); constructibility from Lemma 5.4.3, p. 39, and Theorem 6.7.1 (Grothendieck, Gabber: finite cohomological dimension and preservation of constructibility for $f$ finitely presented with $Y$ quasi-excellent and $\ell$-coprime), p. 55. Bhatt-Scholze's $D_{cons}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat R)$ (Definition 6.5.1, p. 49) asks the reduction to be constructible with perfect values; the category here asks the reductions to be bounded constructible with finite stalks and a uniform amplitude, so the statement is the analogue of Lemma 6.7.2 for this category, with $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\mathfrak m=(\varpi_E)$

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $P_n=A/(\varpi_E^n)$. The coefficient lemmas give a DVR and finite quotients. Its ideals are principal, hence $A$ is Noetherian; $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}A]$ is a finite free resolution of $P_n$. Also $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$, $e>0$, so a power of $\ell$ kills $P_n$. Thus the adic datum applies and the annihilator is invertible on $X,Y$.

proof.text: The perfect-quotient projection formula identifies $F(K)\otimes^L P_n$ with $Rf_{*,n}K_n$. Its compatibility with the reduction unit and the projections of step 2 identifies this map with the finite-reduction comparison in the statement.

proof.text: Finite-type schemes over a field are Noetherian; inverse images of affine opens under $f$ and its diagonal are quasi-compact, so $f$ is qcqs. Apply the finite-coefficient constructibility lemma to each $P_n$ and $K_n$, obtaining bounded constructible etale origins $L_n$ and bounded intrinsic constructibility of the finite images.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; finite-stalk, uniformly bounded version of the pushforward argument

proof.text: The finite relative torsion cohomological dimension supplies some $N\geq0$ with $R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>N$ and every torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$; $f$ is qcqs by step 4. Every $P_1$-module sheaf $M$ is torsion, since a power of $\ell$ kills $P_1$. Coefficient-change vanishing for the ring map $\mathbf Z\to P_1$ says $R^qf_*M=0$ as a $P_1$-module sheaf exactly when it vanishes for the underlying abelian sheaf; equivalently, ringed-topos composition for the identity-topos maps $\mathbf Z\to P_1$, whose direct images are exact restrictions, identifies the underlying abelian derived images. So this $N$ bounds every $P_1$-module sheaf.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; finite-stalk, uniformly bounded version of the pushforward argument

proof.text: For any integer $N$ satisfying the residue bound, apply nilpotent-coefficient devissage with $R=P_n$, $I=(\varpi_E)$ and $I^n=0$. This same $N$ bounds all $P_n$-module etale sheaves.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; finite-stalk, uniformly bounded version of the pushforward argument

proof.text: If $a>b$, each $K_n=0$ and its derived image is zero. For $a\leq b$, apply the etale-origin amplitude lemma to $L_n$ from step 4 and the bound of step 6. If all $K_n$ have range $[a,b]$, it gives range $[a,b+N]$ for every $Rf_{*,n}K_n$, also when $N<0$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; finite-stalk, uniformly bounded version of the pushforward argument

proof.text: For nonempty $X$ of dimension $d$, dimension invariance under every field extension and the torsion-abelian dimension bound give $2d$. Every $P_1$-module sheaf is torsion, and coefficient-change vanishing for $\mathbf Z\to P_1$, as in step 5, gives the module bound. For empty $X$ every input sheaf is zero, so take $N=0$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2; finite-stalk, uniformly bounded version of the pushforward argument

proof.text: Completeness, the identified constructible reductions and their common finite interval satisfy exactly the defining conditions of $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$.
